chapter: Jam sessions, pay and the Vanguard (retyped)
title: Jimmy Ryan's jam sessions and Eddie Condon at work
summary: Hodes says being heard by one's peers was important. He describes Condon's behind-the-scenes work with the press, Ernie Anderson and Milt Gabler, and standing in line to sit in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Man, I got some of the darndest people -- you know, one at a time, one today, one next year, who'd insist on making good on their promises. But those were the early years. By now I'm getting acquainted with Eddie Condon, is in town and I've sat in at Nick's, and all this bumping heads and breaking ground. And I've played at Jimmy Ryan's.

The big thing, to be heard by your peers. It was so important. They had a jam session at Jimmy Ryan's that was run by Eddie Condon and Milt Gabler. Now, Eddie didn't do too much running, he sat on the -- he was either at the bar or he was onstage, pointing his finger, you've got the next chorus, something like that. But behind the scenes, Eddie was a tremendous worker. And and his work was out of the place, digging up things to do.

A story about Eddie that very few people know is that one time there was 18 newspapermen -- I may be exaggerating -- at Nick's to hear the band that he was in, and he picked up the check for every one of them.
Well, he got very good press.
That was why. He was very aware. And his wife was a copywriter for Life or Look or something. She
knew press. And then his brother-in-law, he had the right connections. And whatever his name was, the press agent.

Yeah, Ernie Anderson loved him, just like Milt Gabler loved him. So they made a lot of things possible. So here's this jam session. All I have to do is wait for Earl Hines to step down, some Sunday, Fats Waller, Jimmy Johnson, Joe Sullivan, and then maybe I'll be next. And then here comes Joe Bushkin, where did he come from?
But finally, somebody's pushing and I finally get called up to play, the big moment. Just to sit in.
You had to stand in line.
